detect-names-and-quotes-no-score:
This reads as strongly machine-made. Almost every clause is a listed tell, with little else underneath.

- *"In today's fast-paced digital landscape"* — throat-clearing opener (A4/banned openers), also *landscape* used figuratively (AI vocabulary).
- *"isn't just a tool - it's a partner"* — not-X-but-Y staging (A1), and an em dash used as a hyphen (C5).
- *"It stands as a testament to"* — inflated significance and an avoided plain verb, both in one phrase (B1, B7).
- *"pivotal commitment"* — borrowed weight on an ordinary claim (B8/AI vocabulary); *pivotal* carries no checkable content here.
- *"seamless, vibrant collaboration"* — sales-language pairing, stock adjectives with nothing specific behind them (B4).
- *"empowering teams to unlock their full potential"* — vague declarative closer, the kind of line that would survive being pasted into any other product's copy unchanged (B2).

What's missing is what would make it read as a person: no specific feature, no concrete claim about what the platform does, no named example. It's all staged significance with the content hollowed out — there's nothing here a rewrite could even preserve, because there's no fact underneath the dressing.

Dear Orla,

My name is Dan and I run ScentVerdict, a fragrance review site that I started last year after getting frustrated with how hard it was to find honest reviews of niche perfumes.

We look closely at every fragrance we cover. Each review is based on at least two weeks of wear, and we score longevity, projection and value separately, because a single star rating hides too much. Over the last twelve months we have published 2,400 reviews, and our readers tell us the separate scores are the reason they come back.

I have been following your house for a while and I think your approach to small-batch releases is exactly the kind of story our readers care about. I would love to review your autumn collection, and I would be happy to share our methodology in more detail, including how we handle samples, how we disclose free products, and how we make sure the review is independent of any commercial relationship.

We also run a monthly newsletter that goes to our most engaged readers, and we have a small but growing presence on Instagram and TikTok, where short wear-test videos have done particularly well.

Please do get in touch if this sounds interesting. I would be delighted to set up a call at a time that suits you.

Kind regards,
Dan

First contact (not cut): 223 words. Paragraphs 2 and 4 are the detail a link (a media kit or methodology page) could carry.
